comments.body:
The locale pin in 70f0b17 is too wide: it also changes how command text is read, and that breaks managed-process ownership for non-ASCII paths.

The pin applies to every host-kit `ps` read, including the `pid=,command=` batch read and `readProcessField('command='/'state=')` ([host-process.ts:200](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.ts#L200)). Only `lstart` needs it. BSD/macOS `ps` escapes non-ASCII argv bytes under `LC_ALL=C`: a process started with `/Users/mich/é/ü` prints that path by default and `/Users/mich/M-CM-)/M-CM-<` under the pin. `listHostProcesses` stays unpinned, so one scan now compares UTF-8 command text with escaped text. In [agent-browser-process-record.ts:161-162](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/platform-web/src/agent-browser-process-record.ts#L161-L162), `first.command === last.command && command === first.command` compares the pinned read with the unpinned list. A managed Chrome or agent-browser process with a non-ASCII argv path (a non-ASCII home dir or `--user-data-dir`) fails that filter, so it is never recorded or cleaned up. The command matchers in `judgeProcessIdentity` ([host-process.ts:789-796](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.ts#L789-L796)) and the app-log and recording matchers see the escaped text too. They then either refuse to signal or report the process as reassigned. Before this PR both reads used the same locale and agreed. The rule the code must satisfy: no command text read by host-kit changes encoding between callers, and every `ps` read whose output contains `lstart` is pinned. The set of sites is the `lstart`-bearing reads, meaning `HOST_PROCESS_IDENTITY_PS_ARGS` (sync and async) and `readProcessField` when the field is `lstart=`. Please add a regression that asserts the `pid=,command=` call carries no `LC_ALL` pin.

Not blocking, and fine to take or leave: the new test checks the env argument on mocked `runCmd` calls and expects every call to be pinned, which locks in the problem above, and no test drives `judgeProcessIdentity` or `stopDaemonProcess` with a legacy-locale record against a C-locale read (for example `mar. 17 nov. 19:42:27 2026` against `Tue Nov 17 19:42:27 2026`, expecting `unverified`). `simulator-boot.ts` already defines `C_LOCALE_ENV` and a C-form `lstart` regex, so this PR adds a third spelling; exporting one from host-kit and importing it there would fix that. `env: { LC_ALL: 'C' }` replaces the whole environment. PATH and HOME do not matter, because `ps` is resolved by absolute path, but dropping TZ changes how `lstart` renders, and a record written under a custom TZ would still count as differing. `psStartTimesLocaleMismatch` only matches C form against non-C form, so two different localized renderings still compare as differing, and the comment should state that legacy-only scope.

Could the fix be smaller? Pin only the `lstart` reads, keep command and state reads on default options, keep the 'unknown' rule for legacy records, and put the C-form check beside `processStartTimesDiffer` so `simulator-boot.ts` can reuse it. Nothing else needs to change first. As an optional follow-up, `isAgentDeviceDaemonProcess` in `daemon-process.ts` could use the same comparison, so a legacy-locale daemon can still be stopped after the upgrade.

The Coverage check is failing, but its log ends mid-run in the react-native companion worker tests with no assertion or error line, so it does not point at this PR. Please re-run it. No conflicts. Before merge, narrow the pin to the `lstart` reads and add the unpinned-command regression. The issue's own reproduction (a French-locale daemon with `LC_TIME=C daemon stop`) has not been run on macOS yet, so a live run of that route showing `daemon stop` finding the daemon would close it.

A separate security cross-check of this head, run because process identity decides which process gets signalled, adds two more items before merge:
- **The pin drops the child environment and changes the identity clock** ([ps-start-time.ts:11](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/host-kit/src/internal/ps-start-time.ts#L11)). An explicit exec env replaces the inherited one, so `ps` loses TZ (and LANG) and renders `lstart` in the host zone. With the same explicit TZ on both sides of an upgrade, the new CLI reads a different start time for the same live PID, and `stopDaemonProcess` returns already-exited, which retires a live daemon's registration. Apply `LC_ALL=C` as a final override on top of the effective child environment instead of replacing it.
- **The legacy-locale guard misses real macOS formats** ([ps-start-time.ts:25](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/70f0b17/packages/host-kit/src/internal/ps-start-time.ts#L25)). Under `nb_NO.UTF-8`, macOS `ps` prints the clock with dots, and other locales omit HH:mm:ss entirely. A record written that way does not match the C-form check, so the two renderings count as different lifetimes and a live daemon is again treated as exited. A mismatch should prove exit only when both values are in the same verified format. Otherwise treat the legacy record as unverified, never as gone. Please add a test with a real localized format that has no colon-separated clock, exercised at the `daemon stop` boundary.

Signal authorization still requires an exact identity match, so neither item lets the CLI signal the wrong process. Both make it give up on a live daemon, which is the orphaning bug #4656 reports, now coming from another direction.

Progress at `7ef7ebb`. The locale override is now limited to start-time reads, keeps the effective child environment, and leaves Unicode command reads unpinned. On macOS, a real daemon started under French `LC_TIME` stopped gracefully from a C-locale client. The worker also verified graceful shutdown at a matching explicit `TZ`, and verified that legacy localized records return `identity-unverified` with the process and registration retained.

The cross-time-zone case remains open. The current C-form timestamp has no time-zone provenance. Coverage on this exact head also reports eager-closure growth from `ps-start-time.ts`; this needs a source fix before merge. The cross-zone run and exact-head checks are still pending.

This review covers f88ff09. The newer head 7ef7ebb changes how the locale pin reaches the spawn environment and will get its own delta review; the time-zone and evidence items below do not depend on it. At f88ff09, the earlier command pin and environment replacement findings are fixed, but birth identity and live validation still need work. The real dotted-clock fixture and full macOS run remain outstanding.

Could the process owner give birth tokens locale- and time-zone-independent, identifiable provenance? Starting a daemon in Pacific/Kiritimati and stopping it with TZ=UTC produces different C-shaped strings for the same PID, so [the comparison](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f88ff09/packages/host-kit/src/internal/ps-start-time.ts#L26) can report a live daemon as exited. Conversely, a recycled PID held by a matching daemon can have the same local clock value and pass [signal authorization](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f88ff09/packages/daemon-contracts/src/daemon-process.ts#L38). Both comparisons must treat old unqualified renderings as unknown unless the original lifetime is independently established; keep argv probes separate.

Please remove the redundant [non-ASCII assertion](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f88ff09/packages/host-kit/src/internal/host-process.test.ts#L226) and cover this through the environment-sensitive process reader and real-child stop test. It compares the same constructed string on both sides and passes even when the command read still has the reported regression.

The [takeover test](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f88ff09/packages/daemon-contracts/src/daemon-process-takeover.test.ts#L182) uses a stub executable and synthetic timestamps, so it does not establish graceful stop or live resource ownership. At the fixed head on macOS, start a real detached daemon under fr_FR.UTF-8 in a fresh state directory, capture its PID and token, and run daemon stop --state-dir <dir> --json under LC_TIME=C; show stopped:true, mode:graceful, and PID exit. Repeat across different TZ values. With a separate pre-fix registration from an actual non-C locale, show typed identity-unverified refusal, a live PID, and retained metadata and lock. Run Apple simulator record start and stop through the daemon and show the recorder stops and releases its resource. If the snapshot change remains, show successive requests across provider locales retain the same live snapshot generation.

Not blocking: these can be taken or left: use a valid 21-digit CIM sample for stale Windows fixtures and remove unreachable platform branches; resolve scoped environment overrides once at spawn; bind an installed UTF-8 locale for the real-child Unicode test; use a recorded nb_NO.UTF-8 dotted-clock value; and keep the existing table case instead of the duplicate one-second reuse assertion.

Could the already loaded process capability own POSIX birth-token construction and its sync and async probe policy, with exec resolving scoped overrides once at spawn and the cancellable snapshot provider reusing that policy? A versioned token could identify comparable clocks while historical raw values remain unknown, preserving Linux /proc and Windows CIM tokens; choosing provenance and the legacy refusal rule at the process boundary comes first, while preserving Apple provider cancellation and routing, removing the extra eager import, and consolidating fixtures. No ADR amendment is needed for that ownership.

[Android Smoke Tests](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/actions/runs/44383605765/job/135082109348) passed, but Linux normally uses /proc and does not exercise macOS lstart. [Repo Guards](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/actions/runs/44383605968/job/135082110025) reports R86 on the added process.env capture, and [Coverage](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/actions/runs/44383605968/job/135082109977?pr=4682) reports ten eager-closure assertions with one extra module each. There are no known conflicts. Before merge, fix birth-token ownership and scope, clear R86 and the eager-closure checks at their source, and provide the exact-head macOS receipts.
